html:
A battle fought on 17 September 1176 in a mountain pass west of Konya in central Anatolia, in which the Seljuk sultan Kilij Arslan II ambushed the army of the Byzantine emperor Manuel I Komnenos.

Manuel was marching on Konya, the Seljuk capital, with a large army and a heavy siege train, aiming to take back inner Anatolia, lost after Manzikert. In the narrow pass of Tzybritze the Turks attacked the long column from the heights. The siege engines were lost and parts of the army were cut to pieces. Manuel survived, and the sultan offered peace on fairly mild terms.

The army was not destroyed, and the Byzantines won a battle the next year. But Manuel himself compared the defeat to Manzikert, and his plan to retake the plateau was over. The Komnenian restoration had reached its limit, and the Sultanate of Rum was secure. Within thirty years the empire collapsed in 1204.
sum: A battle fought on 17 September 1176 in a mountain pass west of Konya in central Anatolia, in which the Seljuk sultan Kilij Arslan II ambushed the army of the Byzantine emperor Manuel I Komnenos.
